answer: Each agent must post a bond that is forfeited when independent audits prove it is duplicating identities to claim rewards. Auditors sample actions against a public ledger, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply influence without multiplying bonded capital. The rule works like a wharf charge on every vessel: legitimate newcomers can join, but a sybil operator must lock up funds per identity and risks losing them. Even if shale deposits and zephyr names disguise account links, the economic cost scales with each fake.
